question: Statins lower LDL-cholesterol primarily by inhibiting which enzyme?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Statins are competitive inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in hepatic cholesterol synthesis.
Incorrect. Lipoprotein lipase is the target of fibrates, not statins.
Incorrect. CETP inhibitors (e.g. anacetrapib) are an investigational class; statins do not act on CETP.
Incorrect. Pancreatic lipase is inhibited by orlistat, an anti-obesity drug, not a lipid-lowering drug.

overallFeedback.feedback: Statins are structural analogues of HMG-CoA and competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase — the rate-limiting step of hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis.
Well done. HMG-CoA reductase inhibition reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis, upregulates LDL receptors, and lowers circulating LDL-C.
